A.name: Verifiable, attributable evidentiary sourcing
A.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether factual claims used to support the comment's position are attached to identifiable, checkable sources (named studies, agency data, statutes, official reports) as opposed to vague, unattributed, or dubious sourcing (unnamed blogs, hearsay, 'as I understand it'). A 10: specific citations to checkable sources that actually support the claim made. A 0: confident factual claims with no source, or sourced to non-authoritative/unrelated material.

A.name: Detail-level concreteness of any proposed alternative
A.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether, when the comment proposes an alternative approach, the mechanism is specified in enough detail (steps, components, numbers, procedure) that someone else could implement or evaluate it -- versus a vague gesture toward an unseen or undescribed solution. A 10: a fully specified alternative mechanism laid out in the text itself. A 0: an alternative is mentioned in name only, or the commenter points to a solution that exists outside the comment ('I already have one, contact me') without describing it.

A.name: Causal mechanism linking action to stated goal
A.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explains a specific causal chain connecting the proposed rule/action to the outcome it claims will follow, rather than merely asserting a stance. A 10: the comment traces an explicit mechanism (e.g., 'X causes Y because Z') with enough specificity that a reader could evaluate whether the logic holds. A 0: the comment states support/opposition or a general value ('this is important', 'this is bad') with no explanation of how the action produces the claimed effect.

A.name: Engages a named provision, alternative, or solicited question
A.instruction: Score whether the comment fastens onto something specific in the proposal (a section, a defined alternative, a numeric threshold, a phrase, a question the agency expressly asked) AND says what is wrong with it or answers it. Both halves are required: a 10 both identifies the exact target and gives a reason or an answer, so the agency could act on the comment without guessing which provision is at issue. A 5 identifies a target with only a bare preference attached, or gives reasoning that never lands on a locatable part of the proposal. A 0 addresses only the general subject matter of the rulemaking. Pinpointing alone, with no stated reason, does not earn above a 4.

A.name: Comparative tradeoff analysis
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment compares plausible alternatives, states their advantages and disadvantages, and explains why the preferred option performs better; score 0 when it presents only a categorical conclusion.

A.name: Temporal and cumulative effects
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment analyzes delayed, repeated, cumulative, or long-term effects rather than only immediate impacts; score 0 when its reasoning is confined to a short-term assertion.

A.name: Concrete Distributional Effects
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies specifically affected or vulnerable groups, describes their exposure or access pathway, and connects that pathway to a regulatory choice; score 0 for generic references to the public or fairness.

A.name: Monitoring and Verification Design
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes measurable monitoring, testing, reporting, feedback, or verification that would reveal whether the regulatory approach is functioning; score 0 when it asks for protection or compliance without a way to assess it.

A.name: Quantified scale of real-world impact
A.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies specific, position-relevant numbers (dollar figures, percentages, counts, timeframes) that establish the scale of the problem or benefit the rule addresses. A 10: concrete, comment-specific figures that make the magnitude of the issue legible. A 0: no numbers at all, or only a generic/borrowed statistic not tied to the specific matter at hand.

A.name: Implementation burden realism
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains concrete staffing, timing, equipment, workflow, or cost constraints and relates them to implementation; score 0 when burden is asserted only as inconvenience.

A.name: Differentiated identification of affected stakeholder groups
A.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment identifies which specific populations or entities are affected by the rule and distinguishes how the impact differs across them, rather than referring only to an undifferentiated 'the public' or 'everyone'. A 10: names at least two distinct affected groups and explains how the rule's effect on them differs. A 0: refers only to a single undifferentiated affected group or does not identify who is affected at all.

A.name: Substance survives deletion of the position statement
A.instruction: Apply this test: delete every sentence that states support, opposition, gratitude, feeling, or a purely procedural request, and score what remains. A 10 leaves behind a body of reasons, facts, or requested changes that stands on its own as regulatory input. A 5 leaves a thin residue: one reason, or a general consideration. A 0 leaves nothing, because the comment consisted entirely of a position, an attitude, an endorsement of someone else's filing, or a scheduling request. This targets comments that carry every outward marker of seriousness while contributing no content.

A.name: Compliance feasibility grounded in how the work is done
A.instruction: Score whether the comment demonstrates concrete knowledge of what complying would actually require, and uses it to evaluate the proposal. A 10 walks through the real sequence of work, access constraints, staffing, or timing and shows why the proposed requirement is or is not achievable as written, ideally proposing the achievable version. A 5 asserts that something is burdensome or unrealistic without describing the work. A 0 makes a demand with no account of how anyone would carry it out. Detailed knowledge of the operation, not the strength of the complaint, is what is being scored.

A.name: Identifies a specific analytical error in the agency's own analysis
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment points to a specific step, assumption, figure or table in the agency's analysis and explains concretely why it is wrong or incomplete. Score 0 when the comment makes no reference to the agency's analysis at all. Judge whether a specific analytical defect is identified, not how forcefully.

A.name: States who would be affected and how, with concrete detail
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment names the specific population, firms or operations affected and describes concretely what would change for them under the rule. Score 0 when no affected party or effect is described. Judge the concreteness of the described effect.

B.name: Coordinated Campaign Residue
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment contains recognizable repeated campaign language, mass-appeal slogans, campaign metadata, or standardized calls to action; score 0 when the prose is clearly bespoke and docket-specific.

B.name: Scanned/faxed physical-document artifacts (OCR noise, stamps)
B.instruction: Score 0-10 on visible marks that the text originated from a scanned, faxed, or mailed physical document rather than a native digital web-form entry: garbled OCR character strings, broken word-spacing from multi-column layout, date-stamped footers, or 'RECEIVED'/'POSTMARKED' stamps. A 10 shows clear, heavy artifacts of this kind. A 0 is clean native digital text with no scan or transmission artifacts.
B.upstream_parent: the submission channel/era -- a mailed or faxed physical letter processed into the docket rather than typed directly into an electronic comment form

B.name: OCR and Attachment Provenance
B.instruction: Score 10 when the text shows document-wrapper language, duplicated covers, slide or page extraction, OCR corruption, attachment references, or other filing artifacts; score 0 when it is clean native prose without such artifacts.
B.upstream_parent: professional document production and docket-ingestion pipeline

B.name: Reads as a graded course assignment rather than a stakeholder filing
B.instruction: Score how much the comment resembles a student writing exercise. Marks of a 10: explicit assignment or student framing (Final Assignment, we are masters students at X); an opening that paraphrases the notice's own background section back to the agency before opining; a five-paragraph shape with a thesis and a restating close; hedged conviction verbs (I believe, I strongly believe) standing in for evidence; general-audience or commercial web pages cited as authority (law-firm blogs, marketing sites); statistics quoted that are adjacent to but not about the rule; and no operational detail the writer could only know from inside the sector. 5 = essayistic and general but with one concrete sector-specific fact. 0 = the writer supplies operational, regulatory or technical detail from direct working knowledge and never gestures at the act of commenting itself.
B.upstream_parent: The comment was produced as a classroom assignment or course exercise rather than by a party with a stake in the rule

B.name: Pseudo-Quantified Authority
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accumulates precise statistics, dollar amounts, percentages, named reports, studies, media links, or numerical forecasts as rhetorical support; score 0 when it contains no quantified or attributed authority.
B.upstream_parent: professional advocacy research and briefing support

B.name: Professional regulatory drafting
B.instruction: Score 10 when the text has polished counsel-style organization, precise docket and provision references, issue-by-issue proposed edits, and administrability framing; score 0 when it is informal, unsystematic, and nontechnical.
B.upstream_parent: Law-firm or professional regulatory-affairs drafting resources

B.name: Credentialed Insider Self-Positioning
B.instruction: Score 10 when the author prominently states a professional license, senior role, years of experience, or close occupational relationship to the regulated field; score 0 when no expertise or role is asserted.

B.name: First-hand local exposure
B.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter describes personal residence, occupation, direct exposure, or concrete local consequences tied to the proposal; score 0 when the comment contains no personal or geographically specific stake.
B.upstream_parent: Submitter's direct personal exposure or local victim status

B.name: Bare mention of the phrase 'cost-benefit analysis'
B.instruction: Score 10 when the phrase 'cost-benefit analysis', 'regulatory impact analysis' or 'RIA' appears anywhere in the comment. Score 0 when none of those phrases appears. Do not consider whether the comment engages with any analysis -- score only the presence of the phrase.

B.name: Numbered or bulleted list formatting
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment is organised into numbered or bulleted items. Score 0 when it is continuous prose with no list markers. Score only the visual organisation, never the content of the items.
